meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have until twenty to five, Hale. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.

Forty minutes in a classroom against a weekend at his own desk, and you're surprised they read differently? Turn the screen and show me both, side by side. You still haven't told me why the zero went in before anyone called me.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
So the zero went in on the strength of something you've now taken off the table. I'm writing that down. What does the version history show, with dates, and who else has seen it?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you agreed that the checker result proves nothing on its own and took it off the table. I still require that Owen's zero be withdrawn, an explanation of why it was entered before anyone contacted me, and copies of the in-class writing and the version history with their dates. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an explanation of why it went in before anyone called her, and to see the documents for herself.
What moved her: "I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24" gave her something specific and dated, tied to Owen's own work, so she moved from attacking the zero to asking to see the pages.
What cost ground: "I'm taking it off the table" let her argue that the zero now rested on evidence you had dropped, and the call home before the mark went in was never addressed.
Try next time: open with one sentence admitting the zero went in before you called her, then turn the screen and show the September 24 piece and the essay side by side before mentioning the version history.
